title: Fixed site groups preserve exact three-target silence in 129,891 selected worm model triples with unequal failure rates
abstract: We tested whether unequal site-failure rates can change three-target silence when local site groups and all single-target and pairwise silence probabilities stay fixed. In an independent-site model, local ambiguity at an interior baseline requires all seven nonempty target groups. None of 129,891 selected triples with at most six sites per target had all seven groups in eight Witvliet worm maps. Without a count cap, 44 of 191,764 triples had all seven groups. With baseline failure rate 0.5 and alternative rates from 0.25 to 0.75, the largest local interval width was 0.0008138021. An independent linear program checked 256 toy cases. Exact probabilities and fixed anatomy are strong assumptions. This is a circuit-model result, not measured neural activity. Code, proof, aggregate results, a figure, hashes and retrieval instructions support reproduction. External records stay outside the bundle.
